legend: Peach and Goma have taken up a new hobby recently. Sometimes they decide to get together to look at a number x%%ZSMJ0%% and compute x⊕(x+1)%%ZSMJ1%%, where ⊕%%ZSMJ2%% is the bitwise XOR operator. Today they computed this value for all integers from A%%ZSMJ3%% to B%%ZSMJ4%% inclusive, and Peach and Goma are curious about their results. For a given number M%%ZSMJ5%% they would like you to find the number of integers x%%ZSMJ6%% (A≤x≤B%%ZSMJ7%%) such that x⊕(x+1)≥M%%ZSMJ8%%.
input: The first line contains one integer, T%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤T≤103)%%ZSMJ10%%, the number of test cases. Then T%%ZSMJ11%% test cases follow.
Each test case has a single line with the integers A%%ZSMJ12%%, B%%ZSMJ13%%, M%%ZSMJ14%% respectively, where (1≤A≤B≤109%%ZSMJ15%%, 1≤M≤109%%ZSMJ16%%).
output: T%%ZSMJ17%% lines with one integer each denoting the number of integers x%%ZSMJ18%% (A≤x≤B%%ZSMJ19%%) such that x⊕(x+1)≥M%%ZSMJ20%% for each test case.
note: Note that 3⊕4=7%%ZSMJ21%%, 4⊕5=1%%ZSMJ22%%, and 5⊕6=3%%ZSMJ23%%, therefore there are two integers where the computed value is greater than 2%%ZSMJ24%%.
